raw_response:
I am 73 now, farming alone on 3 mu. My body is not what it was, so I keep things simple — what I have done for many years works, no need to change much.

I split my land like this: 2 mu for wheat-maize rotation, 1 mu for cotton on the sandy patch near the road where wheat does not do well. The well is good, water is not a worry, but electricity for pumping costs money so I only irrigate when I must.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed from the agro-supply shop in town — my neighbor Old Wang had good yield with it last year, so I bought the same. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg, 15-15-15) per mu before ploughing, then top-dress with half a bag of urea (about 25 kg) per mu at green-up in spring. That gives roughly 17-18 kg pure nitrogen. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain-filling. I spray once for aphids and once for rust if I see it. I expect about 450 kg per mu, same as last year.

For maize after wheat in June, I direct-seed with the hand planter, hybrid seed (Zhengdan or similar, whatever the shop has). I put one bag of compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. One irrigation if July is dry, one spray for borer. Maize here gives me 500 kg per mu in a normal year.

Cotton is more trouble — more spraying, more picking. But the price is decent. I use one bag of compound plus 15 kg urea split in two, spray 4-5 times for bollworm and aphids, irrigate twice. I get maybe 250 kg seed cotton per mu. At my age picking is slow, so 1 mu is enough.

I plough with the tractor service — 40 yuan per mu, cheaper than me doing it. Rotary for maize since wheat stubble is there.
